author: DFIR_Radar
text:
Java4Shell (CVE-2026-114938) is a heap overflow in HotSpot's AVX-512 Base64 decoder that gives unauthenticated RCE, but only on x86-64 hosts whose CPUs report four specific features. Patch every Java runtime, and let the processor set the order.

- Scope and status: Calif disclosed it on November 17, 2026. Oracle scores it CVSS 3.1 8.1 (High), and Calif scores it CVSS 4.0 9.2 (Critical). Calif demonstrated unauthenticated RCE against default installs of Keycloak, Jira, Confluence, Artifactory, Jenkins and PingFederate. A self-contained PoC that triggers the bug is public, and the per-product exploit chains are held back. As of November 18, Calif reports no in-the-wild exploitation and it is not in CISA KEV. CISA issued an alert urging immediate patching.

- Why the CPU matters: HotSpot swaps in a hand-written Base64 intrinsic chosen at startup from CPUID. The 512-bit AVX-512 VBMI path "miscalculated the padded tail's store mask, causing an out-of-bounds write." All four flags must be present: bmi2, avx512f, avx512bw, avx512vbmi. Calif lists Intel Xeon Ice Lake, Sapphire Rapids, Emerald Rapids and Granite Rapids, plus AMD EPYC and Ryzen from Zen 4 onward. ARM64 is not affected. "Has AVX-512" is not the test: Eclypsium's Skylake Xeon Platinum 8168 lacks avx512vbmi.

- Affected builds and the inventory gap: OpenJDK 17.0.6 and later, plus downstream distributions (Corretto, Temurin, Microsoft Build of OpenJDK, Red Hat OpenJDK, Oracle OpenJDK, Oracle Java SE). Oracle's list also covers the Java 8 Enterprise Performance Pack build 8u511b33-perf. Version numbers differ per distributor, so check the vendor advisory. CISA notes runtimes bundled in third-party apps, container images and appliances may not appear as separate inventory entries, and a package-manager query misses runtimes in app directories or containers.

- Verification traps: the grep of the flags line in /proc/cpuinfo can falsely say "not affected" on older kernels, because they print only flag names they know. In Eclypsium's lab, Ice Lake guests omitted avx512vbmi there while CPUID inside the same VMs showed it. The JVM reads CPUID, so use the cpuid tool on older guests. Then run java -XX:+PrintFlagsFinal -version with the application's own binary and options, and check UseAVX (3 means AVX-512). UseBASE64Intrinsics = true alone does not mean exposed. VMs migrating to newer hosts, or using host CPU passthrough, can flip a system into scope.

- Mitigation: where patching cannot land, -XX:-UseBASE64Intrinsics or -XX:UseAVX=2 removes the vulnerable path. Set it in the app's JVM options or JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS, and confirm with PrintFlagsFinal. UseAVX=2 is x86-64 only, since a JVM on ARM will not start with it. Eclypsium has not measured the performance cost. CISA also suggests validating Base64 input, enforcing size limits and restricting unauthenticated access.

DFIR takeaway: CISA says crafted Base64 can crash the JVM. When HotSpot crashes it writes hs_err_pid<pid>.log, by default in the process's working directory. Collect these files or service-manager crash events from internet-facing Java services, and alert on new ones. An unexpected crash since November 17 on an internet-facing service running an affected build on a CPU with all four features is a reason to open an incident and review the host, not just restart the service. Preserve the hs_err file and any core dump before restarting. Prioritize Jira, Confluence, Keycloak, Artifactory, Jenkins and PingFederate.

#DFIR_Radar

author: me_deepu
text:
Updated nginx for the new HTTP/2 bugs and only did a reload? Check again. A reload keeps the old binary running, and Xint says you need a full restart.

F5 shipped fixes on Nov 18 for 10 NGINX bugs. The worst, CVE-2026-123007, is an integer overflow in HTTP/2 flow control that writes past a heap buffer, and it has been in the code since 1.9.5 in 2015. The only precondition is HTTP/2 on a listener. Rapid7 has a public PoC for unauthenticated code execution as the worker, though it is noisy (roughly 128 GB of HTTP/2 traffic). F5 says no exploitation in the wild so far.

What to fix today:
1. Move to 1.30.7 or 1.31.9 (Plus: 37.0.8.1 or 37.3.0.1)
2. Restart the service, then confirm the running version
3. Can't patch yet? Set http2 off on exposed listeners, knowing it covers only 2 of the 5 RCEs
4. Alert on "worker process exited on signal" in error logs

Don't forget the nginx copies inside your container images. How many of those have you counted?

https://t.co/sWEJ8AocVI

author: GoPlusSecurity
text:
🚨 OpenJDK “Java4Shell” Vulnerability Alert

On November 17, 2026, Oracle and the OpenJDK project released security updates addressing CVE-2026-114938, a memory corruption vulnerability dubbed Java4Shell. The flaw affects HotSpot’s AVX-512 VBMI-accelerated Base64 decoding intrinsic and can lead to heap data disclosure, JVM crashes, and potentially remote code execution (RCE).

Oracle assigned the vulnerability a CVSS 3.1 score of 8.1 (High). A proof of concept and technical details are publicly available, although application-specific exploit chains remain withheld. Developers should assess their exposure and patch as soon as possible.

📌 Affected Versions and Exploitation Conditions

Affected releases include OpenJDK 17.0.6 and later unpatched builds in the Java 17, 21, 25, and 27 release lines. Distributions incorporating the affected code are also impacted, including Amazon Corretto, Eclipse Temurin, Azul Zulu, Microsoft Build of OpenJDK, and Red Hat OpenJDK.

Exploitation typically requires all of the following:

- An affected, unpatched Java runtime.
- An x86-64 processor supporting AVX-512 VBMI and the associated required CPU features.
- The vulnerable Base64 decoding intrinsic active in the JVM.
- Attacker-controlled data reaching the affected Java Base64 decoder.

ARM64 systems and x86-64 systems without AVX-512 VBMI support are unaffected. Standard OpenJDK 8 and 11 are also unaffected. However, certain Oracle Java SE 8 Enterprise Performance Pack releases are affected.

Researchers at Calif demonstrated pre-authentication RCE in controlled environments against Jira, Confluence, Jenkins, Keycloak, Artifactory, and PingFederate, as well as post-authentication RCE against Kafka, Solr, Elasticsearch, Gerrit, and Spinnaker. Exploitability depends on the application and deployment; there is no universal exploit.

🛡️ Security Recommendations

For Oracle JDK, upgrade to the following patched releases or later vendor-supported security updates:

- Java 17: 17.0.21.1
- Java 21: 21.0.13.1
- Java 25: 25.0.5.1
- Java 27: 27.0.1.1
- Oracle Java SE 8 Enterprise Performance Pack: 8u513-perf

For other OpenJDK distributions, follow the respective vendor’s security advisories and install the appropriate patched builds.

Restart affected JVMs after upgrading. For containerized applications, rebuild and redeploy images containing the patched runtime. Update bundled or embedded JREs using the method supported by the product vendor.

author: LearnInvest2026
text:
A bug that sat in nginx for 11 years lets an attacker run code on a server without logging in, as long as HTTP/2 is on.

nginx is the most widely used web server, powering more than 225 million sites per Wiz. Yesterday it fixed 10 vulnerabilities, five of them critical. The worst, CVE-2026-123007, dates back to version 1.9.5 in 2015, and every open-source release through 1.31.8 is affected. In Wiz's tests it worked even on a server serving only static files.

Five teams including Wiz, Rapid7 and Xint found the bugs independently. Xint chained one with a separate Linux kernel bug to get root on the host, even with nginx inside a Docker container. Wiz says it found them with its AI code scanner. It is the third old bug of this class in a month: PHP last month, Java on Tuesday, now nginx.

F5 and the researchers have not seen attacks yet, but exploit code is public on GitHub. Fixed versions are 1.31.9 and 1.30.7. Ubuntu and Debian packages were not updated as of yesterday. Restart fully after upgrading, since a reload leaves the old binary running. If you cannot upgrade yet, turn off HTTP/2.

author: hackerlogs
text:
‼️ URGENT: Ruby just patched 7 memory bugs in its Regexp engine and String case conversion, and the official advisory says PoCs already turn some of them into remote code execution. If your app changes the case of untrusted text or compiles patterns from user input, upgrade today.

The bugs, per @rubylangorg: a one-byte heap overflow and an integer overflow when changing the case of strings in single-byte encodings like ISO-8859-1 and Windows-1252, a double free and a heap overflow in Regexp compilation, a heap overflow in Regexp#to_s, and two out-of-bounds reads in case-insensitive matching. GitHub rates the case-conversion overflow Critical. CVE IDs are still pending, so track the GHSA IDs.

The AI angle: 4 of the 7 were reported by Stephan Lipp of @ADALogics together with @AnthropicAI. That is a second language runtime this week with AI-assisted memory bugs, after Java4Shell. @tqbf is already calling a race to the first public PoC for the 'ß' case-conversion bug.

Blast radius: Ruby 3.3.13 and earlier, 3.4.0 to 3.4.12, and 4.0.0 to 4.0.9. That is most @rails apps, background workers and Ruby CLIs in production. Ruby 3.2 and older are end of life and get no fix.

Tonight:
1. Upgrade to Ruby 4.0.10, 3.4.13 or 3.3.14, then rebuild Docker base images and CI runners, not just .ruby-version.
2. Until patched, find https://t.co/fvfkUmoefq and Regexp.union fed by user input and escape or allowlist it.
3. Still on 3.2 or older? Treat it as unpatched and plan the jump.

Advisory: https://t.co/DMQlsvhq3I

#Ruby #RubyOnRails #infosec
